[RDSC.9.5] An atom whose body fails protobuf-decode must
cause the loader to error. The error names the atom, the
byte offset, and the protobuf decoder's reason.

A loader **must** refuse with `DS_ERR_DSC_DECODE` a body in which a singular
message field, or a message-typed member of a oneof, occurs more than once, at
any depth, and one in which `proto/header.proto#DscHeader`'s `dsc_sha256`
occurs more than once, since [RDSC.3.6] hashes the artefact with that one
field zeroed. Otherwise a loader **must** hold each body as
protobuf decodes it, whether it decodes with a protobuf library or walks the
bytes itself: a scalar field that occurs more than once holds its last
occurrence, a repeated field holds every occurrence in order, and a oneof holds
only the member that occurs last. No loader then merges two occurrences of a
message, so no loader's answer rests on a library's merge, and two loaders of
one artefact hold the same atom. No conforming compiler writes a field twice
([RDSC.9.9]).
